ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. went

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

4. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

5. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

6. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

7. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

9. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

10. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a joining word

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. quickly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

2. D — went

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

6. B — Where is the library?

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

10. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

11. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

12. A — run

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
